CausalChain: Chronic inflammation -> Activation of CAFs -> ECM remodeling and increased stiffness -> Enhanced mechanotransduction (YAP/TAZ activation plus TGF-β signaling) -> Induction of partial EMT and CSC-like traits, along with immune evasion -> Increased chemoresistance and immunotherapy resistance
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that in cholangiocarcinoma, persistent inflammatory signals trigger activation of CAFs, which in turn remodel and stiffen the ECM. This altered biomechanical environment, together with concurrent cytokine and growth factor signaling, activates both YAP/TAZ and TGF-β mechanotransduction pathways. The ensuing cascade leads to a partial EMT that endows tumor cells with stem cell-like properties and simultaneously creates an immune-suppressive microenvironment, thereby driving both chemoresistance and immunotherapy resistance. By employing cutting-edge methods including 3D culture models, precise biomechanical sensors, high-resolution imaging, and AI-driven data analysis to dynamically monitor these processes, we aim to delineate the interplay between ECM stiffness and mechanosensitive signaling. This approach may facilitate the development of novel combination therapies targeting YAP/TAZ and compensatory pathways to overcome drug resistance.
Abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma is characterized by a multifaceted tumor microenvironment where chronic inflammation triggers cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) activation, leading to extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and increased stiffness. In this refined hypothesis, the stiffer ECM, in synergy with inflammatory cytokines and growth factors, robustly activates mechanotransduction pathways, primarily via YAP/TAZ and additional TGF-β signaling. This cascade induces a partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and fosters the emergence of cancer stem cell-like traits, while concurrently establishing an immunosuppressive microenvironment that culminates in chemoresistance and immunotherapy resistance. We propose leveraging advanced 3D culture systems, high-precision biomechanical sensors, high-resolution imaging, and AI-powered data analytics to quantitatively monitor ECM stiffness and YAP/TAZ/TGF-β dynamics. This integrated technological approach aims to elucidate this spatial and temporal cascade and to identify effective therapeutic windows for combined inhibition of these mechanotransduction pathways.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis proposed that chronic inflammation-induced CAF activation leads to ECM stiffening which, via YAP/TAZ and TGF-β signaling, induces partial EMT and immune evasion contributing to chemo- and immunotherapy resistance. In our refined hypothesis, we retain this fundamental causal chain but enhance its practical applicability by incorporating state-of-the-art technological methods (3D culture systems, biomechanical sensors, high-resolution imaging, and AI-powered analysis) to capture real-time dynamics. Additionally, we explicitly include TGF-β as a complementary pathway alongside YAP/TAZ to provide a more detailed and testable mechanism for dissecting the cascade that drives therapeutic resistance in cholangiocarcinoma.
